subject: City Council Candidates Forum
overview: The Medford Democratic City Committee hosted a forum for Medford City Council candidates to present their platforms and priorities for the upcoming election. Sixteen candidates or their representatives discussed issues ranging from zoning reform and housing affordability to infrastructure maintenance and fiscal transparency.

items.title: Opening Remarks and Forum Rules
items.summary: Bruce Kulik and Phyllis Morrison introduced the event format, noting that each candidate had three minutes to speak without a question-and-answer session.

items.title: Patrick Clerkin Statement
items.summary: Clerkin emphasized the need for a central communication hub for the city to reduce distrust and voiced concerns about the transparency of the current zoning process.

items.title: Nate Merritt Statement
items.summary: Merritt argued for a laser focus on local issues over state or national concerns and advocated for preserving single-family zoning while increasing industrial and commercial activity.

items.title: Matt Leming Statement
items.summary: Councilor Leming highlighted his support for the Proposition 2.5 override to fund schools and roads, along with his work on the affordable housing trust and veteran services.

items.title: Justin Tseng Statement
items.summary: Jessica Taddeo, representing Councilor Tseng, cited achievements in gender-affirming healthcare protection, park modernization, and the codification of non-cooperation with ICE.

items.title: Liz Mullane Statement
items.summary: Mullane proposed applying her professional fundraising and MBA background to diversify city revenue streams and streamline processes for small businesses.

items.title: Anna Callahan Statement
items.summary: Councilor Callahan discussed her efforts to stabilize the budget and her use of volunteer 'democracy teams' to engage residents who do not typically attend public meetings.

items.title: Nick Giurleo Statement
items.summary: Giurleo focused on shifting the tax burden toward the commercial sector and improving council transparency by ending late-running meetings and last-minute agenda changes.

items.title: Miranda Briseno Statement
items.summary: Briseno, a transportation planner, advocated for treating traffic safety as an emergency and utilizing her experience in grant management and union leadership to benefit the city.

items.title: Page Buldini Statement
items.summary: Buldini, running as an unaffiliated candidate, emphasized her experience as a small business owner and called for data-driven decisions on zoning and commercial growth.

items.title: Richard Caraviello Statement
items.summary: Caraviello argued that the current council is attacking neighborhood character through residential rezoning and called for settling long-overdue contracts with first responders.

items.title: Paul Donato Jr. Statement
items.summary: Donato advocated for smarter rezoning targeted at business districts like Mystic Avenue and suggested that infrastructure planning must be a requirement for all new development.

items.title: Melanie Tringali Statement
items.summary: Tringali prioritized neighborhood protection against blanket rezoning and urged for better utilization of 'free cash' for street repairs and public safety staffing.

items.title: Emily Lazzaro Statement
items.summary: Councilor Lazzaro highlighted her advocacy for road safety funding at rotaries, the high school building project, and social services like the Malden Warming Center.

items.title: Zac Bears Statement
items.summary: Councilor Bears spoke in favor of moving the city forward with transformative growth through rezoning and diversifying revenue to avoid regular overrides.

items.title: Trish Schiapelli Statement
items.summary: Schiapelli called for a forensic audit of city finances and criticized the mayor regarding the sale of commercial property to the MBTA.

items.title: Milva McDonald Statement
items.summary: McDonald cited her leadership of the Charter Study Committee and expressed support for a city arts coordinator and residential tax exemptions for owners.
